summary: Microburst pipelining causing GPU starvation and autoscaler stall in dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: ClearView reported a sharp degradation in p50/p99 latency and a throughput collapse for routes pinned to their dedicated pool. The behavior coincided with a burst of many short-lived streaming inference requests from the customer's application. Impact: multiple ClearView routes experienced 5-10x p99 latency increases for ~20 minutes during business hours; customer-facing degradation triggered a support SLA escalation. Timeline: 2026-03-12 09:02 UTC — first alert from customer; 09:05 — support triaged and opened ticket; 09:20 — SRE observed sustained GPU queue depth and slot utilization anomalies; 09:45 — applied temporary mitigation (reserve slots), 10:10 — mitigation restored baseline for ClearView. Observed behavior: - High slot fragmentation: dozens of slots occupied briefly by short streaming sessions, preventing efficient batching. - Autoscaler did not scale up despite high queue depth because burst duration fell below smoothing thresholds. - Serving runtime recorded frequent enqueue/dequeue stalls and occasional KV cache thrashing. - GPUs reported low per-GPU utilization but many pending microbatches queued, suggesting scheduling lock contention rather than raw capacity shortage. Hypothesis: A combination of many short streaming connections (sub-second request durations) and the autoscaler's sampling/decision window caused the controller to miss the microburst signal. The serving scheduler's pipeline/slot allocator prioritized fairness, leading to many partially-filled slots and serialization that prevented efficient kernel batching. Immediate mitigation: - Enabled emergency slot reservation for ClearView (force min_alloc_slots=4) which reduced p99 to baseline within ~25 minutes. - Activated a temporary autoscaler override to respond to queue_depth spikes with a lower smoothing window for the affected pool. - Asked customer to stagger concurrent short streams where possible. Next steps: - SRE to propose autoscaler tuning: introduce a short-window microburst detector and a burst_reservation policy. - Platform to add telemetry for short-lived stream counts and slot fragmentation metric. - Product/SDK team to publish best-practice guidance to customers about connection reuse and batching short streams.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated pool and pin a route to it.
2) From a client, open 500 concurrent streaming requests that send 1-3 tokens then close (simulate sub-second microbursts) over a 2 minute window.
3) Observe slot allocation: many slots will be created but remain partially filled, increasing enqueue latency.
4) Check autoscaler logs — decision will likely not trigger scale-up due to smoothing thresholds.
5) Repeat with longer-lived streams (>=2s) to see autoscaler respond normally and batching efficiency improve.
logs: [2026-03-12T09:18:03Z] scheduler: slot_alloc id=pool-clearview-7 slot=42 state=partial size=3 max_batch=32
investigation_notes: Checked pool metrics: slot_count high, avg_batch_fill low (median ~4 of 32).
Trace of sample traffic from ClearView shows per-connection lifetime median 0.8s and 1-4 tokens per request.
Autoscaler logs show decisions keyed to 60s smoothing window; bursts of 90s total but composed of many <1s streams so peak signal diluted.
No GPU OOMs or CUDA driver errors observed; kernel errors are absent. This is scheduling and batching inefficiency, not raw GPU memory shortage.
Comparing with another pool: pools with streaming-multiplex heuristics were unaffected because they coalesce short streams into persistent sessions.
comments: Priya Nair (Support): Added initial customer timeline and verified baseline restored after slot reservation. Asked for SRE to investigate autoscaler behavior.
Ethan Park (SRE): Reproduced locally using microburst harness. Confirmed autoscaler missed short spikes due to moving average window. Created a safe override to lower sample_window for this pool.
Maya Li (Customer Success): Customer confirmed temporary improvement and appreciated the slot reservation workaround. Asked for guidance to reduce client-side churn.
DevOps (internal): Noted that introducing short-window detectors may increase churn on scaling decisions; recommending conservative default thresholds and opt-in behavior for legacy pools.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: reserved min_alloc_slots for the ClearView pool and applied an autoscaler override to reduce smoothing for microburst detection. Outcome: p99/p50 latencies returned near baseline and customer impact resolved. Follow-ups: (1) Implement microburst detection in autoscaler (RFC scheduled), (2) Add slot_fragmentation and short_stream_count to platform dashboards, (3) Publish customer guidance and SDK helper for connection reuse, (4) Evaluate scheduler heuristics to prefer coalescing short streams into shared sessions. Owner: SRE (Ethan Park) to drive autoscaler change; ETA for RFC and initial prototype: 2026-04-01.
